  %\VignetteIndexEntry{6. Process projects and retain survey relationships}

---

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(appusageR)
data(appusage_demo)
```

Run the 15-source fictional project together with a second, all-failure project.
Projects execute in registry order. File processing within a project can run in
parallel; this tutorial uses one worker for a bounded, portable run.

## Assemble the second project from existing failures

```{r registry}
folder <- system.file("extdata", "synth", package = "appusageR", mustWork = TRUE)
work <- tempfile("appusage-projects-")
failed_raw <- file.path(work, "raw", "ProjectName-DemoFailures_ProjectID-010")
dir.create(failed_raw, recursive = TRUE)
failures <- appusage_demo$sources[appusage_demo$sources$expected_status == "error", ]
stopifnot(nrow(failures) == 5L,
          all(file.copy(file.path(folder, failures$source_relpath), failed_raw)))
good_raw <- scan_appusage_project_root(folder)$project_dir[1L]
projects <- data.frame(
  project_id = c("009", "010"), project_name = c("Demo", "DemoFailures"),
  project_dir = c(good_raw, failed_raw),
  output_dir = file.path(work, c("demo-output", "failures-output")),
  self_report_file = c(file.path(folder, "ProjectID-009-WJXraw-synthetic.xlsx"), NA),
  sheet = c("Survey", NA), sequence_col = c("sequence_id", NA),
  upload_col = c("upload", NA), submit_time_col = c("submitted_at", NA))
config <- appusage_config(execution = list(progress = FALSE, strict = FALSE))
batch <- run_appusage_projects(projects, file.path(work, "batch"),
  config = config, workers = 1L, continue_on_error = FALSE)
batch$projects[, c("project_id", "status", "action", "n_sources", "source_issues")]
stopifnot(identical(batch$projects$project_id, c("009", "010")),
          all(batch$projects$status == "completed_with_source_issues"),
          identical(as.integer(batch$projects$source_issues), c(5L, 5L)))
```

`strict = FALSE` retains per-source diagnosed failures. `continue_on_error = FALSE`
stops the collection on a project-level failure; a complete set of diagnosed
invalid inputs is not such a failure. Batch checkpoints belong in a directory
separate from all input and output projects.

## Inspect full-project results and survey links

```{r survey}
# Reuse the saved manifest and configuration, including questionnaire settings.
result <- run_appusage_workflow(project_dir = projects$output_dir[1L])
stopifnot(sum(result$first_level$status == "success") == 10L,
          sum(result$first_level$status == "error") == 5L,
          sum(result$qc$qc_status == "success") == 10L,
          sum(result$qc$pass_qc %in% TRUE) == 5L,
          sum(result$qc$qc_status == "not_run") == 5L)
names(result)
```

The general matching function can also link an in-memory questionnaire to the
same resolved source manifest. The manifest retains failed uploads with missing
proc-2 paths, so they have an explicit downstream status.

```{r relationships}
first <- result$first_level
second <- result$second_level
manifest <- data.frame(source_file = first$source_file,
  second_level_rda = second$second_level_data_file[
    match(first$data_file, second$first_level_data_file)])
linked <- match_appusage_self_report(appusage_demo$survey, manifest = manifest,
  project_dir = projects$output_dir[1L], sequence_col = "sequence_id",
  upload_col = "upload", submit_time_col = "submitted_at")
survey <- linked$matched_self_report
expected <- appusage_demo$expected_links
stopifnot(nrow(survey) == 17L,
          identical(survey$survey_id, expected$survey_id),
          identical(survey$moSens_match_status, expected$expected_match_status),
          all(vapply(names(appusage_demo$survey), function(column)
            identical(survey[[column]], appusage_demo$survey[[column]]), logical(1))))
table(survey$moSens_match_status)
survey[survey$sequence_id == "109", c("survey_id", "moSens_match_status", "moSens_data_dir")]
linked$file_matches
```

Eight questionnaire rows match. The remaining nine comprise five uploads without
proc-2, one filename mismatch, one sequence mismatch, one missing upload and one
unresolved upload. All 17 rows and their original values survive. Sequence `109`
has two source uploads: both caches remain, while generic matching uses export
priority and submission-time proximity to select a candidate. This is distinct
from a study-specific reupload/retest/original priority policy.

`run_appusage_project_workflow()` combines folder/workbook discovery with these
operations; `demo("synthetic-project", package = "appusageR", ask = FALSE)` runs
that adapter with two file workers. For your own collection, supply the explicit
registry and questionnaire column names rather than relying on this layout.

## All-failure delivery and resume

```{r failures}
failed <- run_appusage_workflow(project_dir = projects$output_dir[2L])
stopifnot(nrow(failed$first_level) == 5L,
          all(failed$first_level$status == "error"),
          !any(failed$second_level$second_level_status == "success"),
          all(failed$qc$qc_status == "not_run"), all(is.na(failed$qc$pass_qc)))
failed$first_level[, c("source_file", "status", "error_message")]
reports <- lapply(projects$output_dir, validate_appusage_project, verify = "content")
stopifnot(all(vapply(reports, function(x) isTRUE(x$complete), logical(1))))
print(reports[[2L]])
```

Both projects pass content delivery. Single-project and collection resume retain
all five terminal failures. On an unchanged collection, each project reports
`skipped_complete` with action `reuse`; its source issues remain visible.

```{r collection-resume}
again <- run_appusage_projects(projects, file.path(work, "batch"),
  config = config, workers = 1L, continue_on_error = FALSE)
again$projects[, c("project_id", "status", "action", "error")]
stopifnot(all(again$projects$status == "skipped_complete"),
          all(again$projects$action == "reuse"),
          identical(as.integer(again$projects$source_issues), c(5L, 5L)),
          all(again$projects$workflow_elapsed_sec == 0),
          isTRUE(validate_appusage_project(projects$output_dir[2L], verify = "content")$complete))
```

The earlier `invalid 'file' argument` on all-failure collection resume is fixed:
the protection check accepts the all-missing path column read from the saved CSV.
Existing scientific artifacts retain the same content and compatibility checks.
Collection reuse runs no parsing, scientific processing, QC or questionnaire
matching stages; it preserves the saved diagnoses and results.

| All-failure input | Diagnosis |
|---|---|
| Empty mixed export | Headers exist but contain no data |
| Unrecognized text | No supported export content |
| Zero-byte upload | No bytes to parse |
| Binary content with `.txt` suffix | Binary signature rather than text |
| Incomplete interval structure | Critical missing end-time evidence |

The second project accounts for 5/5 sources but has 0/5 successful research
outputs and zero evaluated QC records. Its delivery check passes because the
terminal diagnoses and required downstream states are intact. It supplies no
analytic sample. This is why delivery completeness and QC use different
denominators.

```{r cleanup}
unlink(work, recursive = TRUE)
```
